facts.statement: Born Stirling 1796, died 1888; army service in the Peninsula and America.
Ordained after military service; Chaplain-General of the Forces, 1844–75.
Wrote The Subaltern and accounts of British campaigns in America.

interpretation.note: Interpretation of the documented life and works; no claim of personal acquaintance from shared themes.

appraisal.note: AETERNUS editorial judgement; not presented as a historical quotation.

en.tagline: The soldier who became the army’s chaplain and historian.
en.intro: Gleig wrote with the memory of a young officer and the later vocation of a clergyman. His long career brought campaigning, religious service and historical authorship into one life.
en.orientation: The books of personal military experience have a different standing from his later historical compilations. The witness’s closeness is strongest where he writes of service he knew.
origin: Born in Stirling, he left his early university course for the army. Service in the Peninsula and America preceded his return to study and ordination.
career: He later became Chaplain-General of the Forces, holding the office from 1844 to 1875. Writing accompanied this institutional career across many years.
literature: The Subaltern and the American campaign narratives draw the reader towards marching, fighting and the perceptions of a junior officer. Their perspective is necessarily narrower than that of a later strategic history.
en.legacy: Gleig preserves the voice of service across a remarkable change of vocation. His works show how military experience could be carried into the religious and literary institutions of nineteenth-century Britain.
en.bridge: The narratives restore the campaign at the scale of the serving officer’s day.
